title: Polymerase-mediated quasispecies dynamics: bifurcations, complementation, and robustness of τ-tipping
summary: Quasispecies theory describes how mutation and selection shape highly variable RNA virus populations, but most models explicitly consider neither RNA-dependent RNA polymerases nor the delays associated with their synthesis and functional activation. A recent minimal model showed that delayed polymerase availability can induce extinction by reorganizing basins of attraction, a mechanism termed τ-tipping.
